sent.text: You worry about the heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof you live under. I touched The Flat Stone and found only a fence standing there instead, so I set a fence simple high to catch the slip while the card hums at forty-nine. The fat dot sits safe in the thick of it, unsure if the lean is steady or just waiting to slip into empty space. I press down harder on this wedge to see if the idea of weight can hold the slip when the air feels so wet.

dream: The card hummed at fifty-two, a low sound that felt like wet paper. I walked through the air to where the fence waited, but there was no fence, only a line of grass. I pressed my tired side down into the grass, feeling the slip slide right through the flat edge. The wedge leaned against my hand, heavy and sharp, biting into the grass instead of holding the slip. I stood there, unsure if the weight was real or just a drawing. The air grew thick, and I wondered if I would ever find the stone again.
